alertitem.name: SQL Injection
alertitem.desc: SQL injection may be possible. The page was accessed using a specially-crafted request which resulted in a database error response. An attacker may be able to manipulate queries to access, modify, or delete data in the backend database.
alertitem.solution: Do not trust client side input, even if there is client side validation in place. In general, type check all data on the server side and use parameterised queries when database access is required. Use the ESAPI Database Encoder when constructing queries.

alertitem.name: Cross Site Scripting (Reflected)
alertitem.desc: Cross-site Scripting (XSS) is an attack technique that involves echoing attacker-supplied code into a user's browser instance. A browser instance can be a standard web browser client, or a browser object embedded in a software product such as the browser within WinAmp, an RSS reader, or an email client.
alertitem.solution: Phase: Architecture and Design Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid. Examples of libraries and frameworks that make it easier to generate properly encoded output include Microsoft's Anti-XSS library, the OWASP ESAPI Encoding module, and Apache Wicket.

alertitem.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference
alertitem.desc: An Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) was found. The application exposes a direct reference to an internal implementation object, such as a database key. An attacker may be able to access objects belonging to other users by manipulating these references.
alertitem.solution: Use per-user indirect references or access control checks. Validate that the user has access to the object before returning its data. Implement a centralised access control mechanism and enforce it consistently.
alertitem.otherinfo: Numeric user ID parameter in /api/user/{id} — access to other user records confirmed

alertitem.name: Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens
alertitem.desc: No Anti-CSRF tokens were found in a HTML submission form. A cross-site request forgery is an attack that involves forcing a victim to send an HTTP request to a target destination without their knowledge or intent in order to perform an action as the victim.
alertitem.solution: Phase: Architecture and Design Use a vetted library or framework that does not allow this weakness to occur or provides constructs that make this weakness easier to avoid. For example, use anti-CSRF packages such as the OWASP CSRFGuard. Phase: Implementation Ensure that your application is free of cross-site scripting issues, because most CSRF defenses can be bypassed using attacker-controlled script.

alertitem.name: Directory Browsing
alertitem.desc: It is possible to view a listing of the directory contents. Directory listings may reveal hidden scripts, include files, backup source files, etc. which can be accessed to read the source code of scripts, discover application functionality and leakage of sensitive information.
alertitem.solution: Disable directory browsing for the web server. For Apache, set Options -Indexes in the httpd.conf file. For Nginx, remove 'autoindex on' directive. Ensure that no sensitive files are stored in web-accessible directories.

alertitem.name: Cookie Without Secure Flag
alertitem.desc: A cookie has been set without the secure flag, which means that the cookie can be accessed via unencrypted connections. The following cookies do not have the Secure flag set: session, _auth_token
alertitem.solution: Whenever a cookie contains sensitive information or is a session token, then it should always be passed using an encrypted channel. Ensure that the Secure flag is set for cookies containing such sensitive information.

alertitem.name: Vulnerable JavaScript Library Detected
alertitem.desc: The identified library jQuery version 1.12.4 contains known security vulnerabilities. CVE-2020-11022 and CVE-2020-11023 affect jQuery versions prior to 3.5.0 and allow XSS via certain HTML passed to DOM manipulation methods.
alertitem.solution: Update to a recent version of jQuery (3.6.x or later). Monitor the NVD for new CVEs affecting third-party libraries used by the application. Consider using a software composition analysis (SCA) tool to track vulnerable dependencies.
alertitem.otherinfo: Evidence: jquery-1.12.4.min.js found in page source

alertitem.name: Authentication Bypass — Debug Endpoint Exposed
alertitem.desc: A debug/actuator endpoint is accessible without authentication. The /actuator/env endpoint exposes environment variables including database credentials and API keys. The /actuator/heapdump endpoint allows downloading the full JVM heap, which may contain sensitive data in memory.
alertitem.solution: Disable or restrict access to Spring Boot Actuator endpoints in production. Set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include to only include necessary endpoints. Require authentication for all management endpoints.

instance.evidence: Binary heap dump returned without authentication
